cards.title: What's going on
cards.text: Your child's condition is called Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy, often shortened to HCM, and it is linked to a gene called MYH7 [Ec8c1e4e, E53f2d13]. Genes are like instruction pages that tell the body how to build and run parts of itself, and MYH7 carries instructions for a protein that heart muscle uses to squeeze and relax [E14a5c39]. Changes in this gene are one of the most common causes found in families with this condition [E4c43191]. Researchers describe the problem as happening in the sarcomere, which is a tiny working part inside heart muscle cells [E1ed33e0, E94b588b]. One well-studied gene change, called p.R403Q, is linked to the heart muscle squeezing harder than usual and to HCM starting [E104959c, Eff502cb]. Specific changes in the MYH7 gene, including p.Met515Val, p.Ala729Pro, and p.Lys611Asn, have been recorded as disease-causing for this condition [Eaf9f32c, E529adb0, E9a10458]. Children with this condition have been recorded as having features such as narrowing below a heart valve, an uneven heartbeat, a thicker wall between the heart's pumping chambers, heart failure signs, and sudden death as an associated feature [E73fcc53, E0582de0, Ef27c7d9, E713082f, Ee4ff1aa]. This condition can be passed down in families in a pattern called autosomal dominant, meaning a change in just one copy of the gene can be enough [E33b64f2].

cards.title: How it compares to other conditions
cards.text: A paper does note that several other genes besides MYH7, including MYBPC3, TNNT2, TNNI3, TPM1, ACTC1, MYL2, and MYL3, have also been linked to causing this same condition in other families [E7d9c4fa]. Another paper reports that MYBPC3 changes are also a leading cause of HCM and that these cases can look the same as HCM caused by MYH7 changes [Edaf4fc6].

cards.title: What exists already
cards.text: There are patient groups focused on this condition, including the Cardiomyopathy Patient Council based in Ireland and Cardiomyopathy UK based in the United Kingdom [E5a3bbe2, Eb426000]. A trial in the United States is currently recruiting to compare a medicine called BHB-1893 with a medicine called Metoprolol for people with symptoms of obstructive HCM [E03eaf11, Ea232fc2, E19a14a7, Ee56b7c4]. Two other trials in the United States, run by Bristol-Myers Squibb, are looking at a medicine called Mavacamten for obstructive HCM, though neither is currently recruiting [Ea2ef61b, E3c4c78d, Eba1ca1e, E472ceb8, E3f08204, Ed3a547d]. A study called NHLBI SESAME, looking at a device-based procedure for this condition in the United States, has not yet started recruiting [E73a3f2f, Ea264cea, E6184941]. NIH NHLBI and NIH VA are funding research into how MYH7 gene changes affect heart muscle cells, with researchers Kai-Chun Daniel Yang, Clayton E Friedman, and Tanner O Monroe leading these grants [E76283dd, E3bc422d, E923883a, Ea5fb710, E2e9cb67, Eb7a841e, E91deb44, Ed7a10a1, E39db6ec, E288ee21, E809eb01, E78815a9, Efa5df04, E58eecef, E086f488]. A paper that mentions this condition was authored by researchers Yanling Wang and Ying Sun, looking at how a gene-editing approach affects the non-changed copy of a gene in dominant conditions [E5bcedec, E82620c1, E53a17cf].

cards.title: Possible next steps
cards.text: A first step could be reaching out to the Cardiomyopathy Patient Council, a patient group based in Ireland that the atlas connects to HCM (MYH7), to learn more and connect with other families [E5a3bbe2]. You could also contact Cardiomyopathy UK, a patient group based in the United Kingdom that the atlas connects to HCM (MYH7), for information and support [Eb426000].
